summary: Frontend E2E tests for Doctor Assignment feature. All 8 scenarios pass end-to-end after resolving test-side timing/session issues. Backend endpoints (/api/doctors, /api/profile/doctor, /api/admin/patients, /api/admin/patients/{id}/doctor, /api/doctor/patients) are correct and produce the expected behavior. Verified: patient self-selection via Settings 'My Doctor' card (data-testid=my-doctor-card / my-doctor-select) persists across reload; transferring away from Dr. Layla immediately removes the patient from her Doctor Portal list and re-selecting her restores it; a freshly registered patient (unassigned) is invisible to Dr. Layla in both /doctor and the /doctor/schedule new-encounter dropdown (data-testid=encounter-patient-select); admin /admin/assignments page renders the table with per-row dropdowns (assign-doctor-select-{user_id}), shows the unassigned-banner (1 patient), records 'chosen by' correctly (patient for Omar, migration for the rest), and assignments persist across reload; after admin-assigns the new patient to Layla she can see and open the detail card; admin-clearing removes them from Layla's list; access control blocks patients and non-admin doctor Dr. Layla from the Assignments nav item and shows admin-access-denied on direct /admin/assignments visit; regression — Doctor Schedule still lists 17 encounters with badges and encounter detail page opens, and admin's Doctor Portal correctly bypasses assignment filtering (13 patients incl. Hashim/HAshim).
action_items: Consider surfacing /doctor/patients load errors instead of silently swallowing them in DoctorPortal.jsx (.catch(() => {})). During auth-refresh races the list currently renders empty with no user feedback.
critical_code_review_comments: DoctorPortal.jsx uses `.catch(() => {})` on the /doctor/patients fetch — a transient 401 (which does happen on the first request right after login while the cookie is being set, then succeeds after axios interceptor triggers /auth/refresh) can leave the list stuck empty because there's no error state and no retry. Recommend surfacing an error state or explicitly re-fetching once user context is confirmed.

MyDoctorCard.jsx and DoctorPortal.jsx both read `user.role`/`user.assigned_doctor_user_id` at mount but the doctor list from /api/doctors is async — if that request fails silently (also `.catch(() => {})`), the select renders with only 'No doctor chosen' and no indication of failure. Same UX concern as above.
AdminAssignments.jsx works well; the unassigned-banner correctly shows count and pluralization. Consider disabling the row while savingId matches (already done via `disabled` on select) — good.
assert_doctor_can_access_patient / admin bypass on /doctor/patients works as designed — admin sees all 13 patients incl. throwaway unassigned user; verified end-to-end.
seed_data_creation: Registered one throwaway patient during Test 3 (email=testpatient_1787125089@sihha.ai, user_id=user_95e5ff547161). No delete endpoint exists; left it in an Unassigned state per instructions. Omar was left assigned back to Dr. Layla (verified via /api/admin/patients).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature is fully working. Data state at end of run: Omar Farouk → Dr. Layla Haddad (chosen by 'patient'); all migration patients → Dr. Layla Haddad; testpatient_1787125089@sihha.ai remains Unassigned (visible only to admin at /admin/assignments). If flaky UI test needs re-run: use fresh_login pattern that (a) clicks logout button (b) clears cookies (c) navigates to /auth with networkidle wait, and always wait_for_timeout(3000) after login/goto('/doctor') because /auth/me + /doctor/patients race with cookie set — the DoctorPortal's silent-catch means the UI shows empty list forever if the first call 401s.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no product bugs found. Any transient empty-list observations during testing were caused by a client-side race: on immediate re-login the first /doctor/patients call can 401 before the new httpOnly cookie is applied, axios interceptor refresh recovers subsequent calls but DoctorPortal's silent `.catch(() => {})` never retries or shows an error, so the initial empty state sticks until a manual reload. Not a business-logic bug but a UX resiliency gap worth fixing.
